title: Per-route fallback request charges misattributed to primary route causing quota burn and penalty-window throttles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: We observed per-route quotas being charged to the original (primary) route when requests were transparently routed to a fallback route/model. This leads to unexpected quota burn on the primary route and triggers penalty/cooldown windows there, causing downstream throttles for customers who never hit the primary model. The bug is in the policy-enforcer's charge attribution: it uses the initial route identity in its debit operation after routing resolution has changed the final target.

Why it matters: Customers see quota exhaustion and throttles on routes they didn't actually serve traffic for. This affects dedicated and hosted tenants with aggressive quota enforcement and has resulted in at least two customer escalations in the last 72 hours.

Observed behavior: When smart routing decides to fallback (capacity or model variant fallback), telemetry shows the request served by fallback model but the meter/debit counters (per-route and per-org) reflect the primary route key. Penalty window and cooldowns are recorded on the primary route.

Expected behavior: The final routed target (post-fallback) should be the canonical charge key for all usage accounting and penalty/credit application. If fallbacks are used, accounting must attribute to the actual serving route or to an explicit shared-billing key per policy.

Hypothesis / root cause: The enforcer evaluates policy and constructs debit keys using request.route_alias early in the pipeline. Smart routing can mutate request.final_route after policy evaluation for fallback decisions. The enforcer's accounting code caches the earlier alias (or uses a request-scoped value) and performs debits with that stale key. Additionally, penalty-window bookkeeping reuses the same stale key which applies cooldowns to the wrong route. Race conditions and cached key lifetimes in the enforcer path are the likely root cause.

Impact scope: High for per-route quota customers. We saw a 12% unexpected quota burn spike across affected orgs and two customer reports of sudden throttles despite using fallback-only traffic. The issue reproduces reliably when fallback is forced via test headers.

Proposed fix: Atomically determine and freeze the final billing attribution key after routing resolution but before any meter/debit operations. Specific actions: (1) Move attribution key computation to routing finalizer; (2) Replace request-scoped mutable alias fields with an immutable billing_key on the request context; (3) Add a guard in the enforcer to assert billing_key == final_route or log and fallback to final_route if mismatch; (4) Add integration tests simulating fallback and verify per-route counters and penalty windows are applied to billing_key.

Rollback / mitigation plan: Gate the attribution change behind a feature flag (billing.fix/fallback-attribution) and ship to canary shards first. As mitigation, deploy a short-term compensating job to reconcile recently misattributed charges (see "mitigation" notes below) and temporarily relax penalty-window enforcement for affected routes while the fix is deployed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a small canary where fallback routing is enabled. 2) Send a batch of requests with header X-Force-Fallback: true to cause routing to select fallback model. 3) Observe per-request logs (request_id) showing final_route=fallback-v1 but meter increments appear under route=primary-v2. 4) Query /internal/metering/route-usage for primary-v2 and fallback-v1; the primary shows non-zero despite fallback serving. 5) Reproduce also by simulating capacity exhaustion to trigger fallback and confirm same misattribution.
observed_behavior: Debit and penalty-window bookkeeping applied to the initial route alias even when final routing served a fallback. Per-route meter counters diverge from actual served route counts.
expected_behavior: All billing debits, meter increments, and penalty/penalty-window state must be attributed to the final serving route (or to an explicit, policy-defined shared billing key).
mitigation: Short-term: 1) Enable an observability alert to detect route mismatch events and notify SRE. 2) Temporarily relax penalty window enforcement for routes with high mismatch metric to avoid customer throttles. 3) Run a reconciliation job to move wrongly-attributed usage from primary route to fallback where safe (see Confluence doc).
tests:
- Unit tests: route alias -> billing_key mapping invariants.
- Integration: end-to-end request through policy -> routing -> enforcer asserting billing_key matches final_route.
- Load test: ensure no performance regression when computing billing_key atomically.
- Regression: replay historical canary traces to ensure reconciliation job correctness.
postmortem_plan: If fix deployed to canary and validated, roll to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24h. After full rollout, run reconciliation for the last 48h of misattributed charges and issue credits where appropriate. Update docs and add a 'billing_key' field to API request logs for easier future debugging.
root_cause: Stale route alias used for debit operations due to ordering: enforcer performed accounting using a request-scoped alias before the routing finalizer updated final_route. Mutable request context and cached key lifetimes allowed incorrect attribution when fallback occurred.

2026-03-01 SRE Team: Added Grafana dashboard linking request_id traces to per-route metering. Noted pattern in ~8 distinct request_ids where final_route != charged_route.
2026-03-02 Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally by forcing fallback via X-Force-Fallback header. Confirmed meter increments attributed to the pre-routing alias. Hypothesis added to description.

2026-03-03 Maya Chen: Created draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1286 that moves billing key computation to routing finalizer and adds assertion in enforcer. Needs review.
2026-03-04 Code Review (Nora Kim): Left comments about atomicity and potential perf impact. Suggested microbenchmark and adding a feature flag.
2026-03-05 Liam O'Connor: Addressed review comments, added feature flag billing.fix/fallback-attribution, and added integration tests simulating fallback path. Pushed new commits.
2026-03-07 QA (Javier Lopez): Canary tests on shard-3 show correct attribution for fallback traffic. Observability alert rate reduced to baseline. Preparing rollout notes.
